findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the cachePoint-TTL capability assertion against the landed evidence (docs/local-dev-env.md:192-202 and story 1aa2): update the Context claim that the TTL difference is 'substantive'/'most likely to bite', since both providers default to a 5-minute TTL and rebar sets no non-default TTL.

S6/0d76 final comment: 'The cachePoint TTL item this ticket deferred to S8 IS NOW ANSWERED, on 1aa2: Bedrock cachePoint takes an OPTIONAL ttl DEFAULTING TO 5 MINUTES ... The premise that Bedrock "carries no TTL" was wrong; there is no substantive difference to carry forward.'
findings.finding: The plan asserts as an established fact that the missing cachePoint TTL is the substantive envelope difference 'most likely to bite' and that Bedrock's cachePoint 'carries NO TTL', but landed repo prior art refutes this: the cachePoint ttl defaults to 5 minutes — the same as Anthropic's cache_control — so there is no substantive difference. AC6 is built around investigating a question the codebase already answered.
findings.location: Context / Problem ('ONE ENVELOPE DIFFERENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE ... Bedrock's cachePoint carries NO TTL') and AC6 ('Whether the missing Bedrock cachePoint TTL causes any observable difference is STATED')
scenarios: Implementer spends the story's investigation budget re-deriving a TTL conclusion that repo docs and story 1aa2 already establish
The plan's stated risk model ('the thing most likely to bite') misdirects attention from real risks
findings.suggested_fix: Restate the Context bullet as 'the cachePoint TTL was previously flagged as a potential difference but 1aa2 measured it defaults to 5m on both providers — no substantive difference', and re-scope AC6 to confirming that resolved finding rather than treating it as open.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the cachePoint-TTL claim with S6 (0d76) and docs/local-dev-env.md: state that Bedrock's cachePoint ttl is optional and defaults to 5m (same as Anthropic), so there is no substantive TTL difference, and reword AC #6 to confirm that resolved fact rather than to 'find out if that assumption is wrong'.
evidence: Plan asserts: 'Bedrock's cachePoint carries NO TTL where Anthropic's cache_control carries ttl:"5m". Latent today … this story is the cheapest place to find out if that assumption is wrong.'

Contradicted by S6 (0d76) final AC-verification comment: 'Bedrock cachePoint takes an OPTIONAL ttl DEFAULTING TO 5 MINUTES — the same default Anthropic cache_control applies. The premise that Bedrock "carries no TTL" was wrong; there is no substantive difference to carry forward.'

The plan's own deliverable docs/local-dev-env.md:192-196 already states the ttl is 'optional and defaults to 5 minutes — the same default Anthropic's cache_control applies', i.e. the plan text and its documentation disagree.
EVIDENCE CLASS: Contradicted (a sibling story's recorded measurement and the plan's own docs falsify the 'no TTL' capability assertion).
findings.finding: The 'already established' block asserts as a settled do-NOT-re-measure fact that Bedrock's cachePoint 'carries NO TTL' and that this is 'the one SUBSTANTIVE envelope difference' — but the sibling story the plan cites (S6 / 0d76) recorded that premise as refuted (cachePoint's ttl is optional and defaults to 5 minutes, the same default Anthropic applies), and the plan's own docs/local-dev-env.md already documents the corrected behaviour. AC #6 is built on a difference the cited evidence says does not exist.
findings.location: Context §'What is already established' final bullet ('ONE ENVELOPE DIFFERENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE …'); Acceptance Criteria line 6 ('Whether the missing Bedrock cachePoint TTL causes any observable difference is STATED')
scenarios: An implementer takes the 'substantive difference' premise at face value and spends effort chasing a TTL divergence that the cited evidence already resolved to 'no difference'.
AC #6's evidence ('STATED, with evidence either way') is discharged against a premise that is already known-false, producing a recorded 'finding' that is actually a non-issue.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 'ONE ENVELOPE DIFFERENCE IS SUBSTANTIVE' bullet with the resolved fact (Bedrock cachePoint ttl is optional, default 5m, matching Anthropic's cache_control default — established on 0d76/1aa2), and retarget AC #6 to 'confirm no observable TTL difference (5m default on both paths), with evidence.'

findings.finding: The leaf S7b's What/Scope is not a subset of its DECLARED parent S8 (eb6e); it is disjoint from S8 and disclaims S8's only deliverable surface. S8's entire plan is the PRODUCTION cutover under infra/ (Scope: infra/compose/, infra/scripts/fetch-secrets.sh, infra/scripts/observability.sh, infra/runbooks/; ACs: a real Gerrit LLM-Review Bedrock vote, CloudWatch alarm, kill-switch runbook, denied-access drill, container env). S7b instead delivers LOCAL developer-gate dogfooding, local LLM config, and docs/local-dev-env.md, and explicitly states 'This story must not touch infra/' with an AC 'Nothing under infra/ is modified'. So the leaf delivers work the declared parent's plan does not contain and refuses the parent's sole subject — stepping outside the declared parent's contract rather than narrowing it. The work IS contained by the GRANDPARENT epic 061c (its AC 'rebar review-plan and rebar verify-completion both run green against Bedrock in a live env-gated check', and approach step 5 'Dogfood on the review bot'), which indicates the correct container for S7b is the epic (a direct-story sibling of S8 and S9), not S8.
findings.location: S7b Scope / 'Explicitly out of scope' vs parent eb6e (S8) Scope+ACs; parent_id points at eb6e
scenarios: An implementer takes eb6e as the containing contract and expects S7b to advance the production cutover, but S7b delivers only local-machine evidence and forbids touching infra/ — the parent's stated deliverables are neither delivered nor narrowed by this child.
A completion check compares S7b against its declared parent eb6e and finds no overlap, because the true container is the epic 061c one level up.
findings.suggested_fix: Change S7b's parent from eb6e (S8) to 061c (the epic). The epic's ACs and approach step 5 already contain the local-gate Bedrock dogfooding S7b delivers, so S7b becomes a faithful narrowing of the epic and a sibling of S8/S9, and the 'must not touch infra/' disclaimer no longer contradicts the parent's scope.
